open_questions: Need on-target photometry to confirm whether the 11.4 d signal is coherent and stable at the same depth across independent data
dossier.public_summary: A 4452 ppm dip repeats every 11.4 days but its measured depth triples between sectors and the light curve shows a large brightness swing outside the dip. The fit also conflicts with the star's density. Together this points to a blended variable or systematic false alarm rather than a stable planet transit around the target.

reasons.why: Depth varies strongly between sectors (1443 ppm in sector 24 vs 5893 ppm in sector 50 and 5091 ppm in sector 78, chi2 17.17 dof 3) and sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with p_constant 0.0002806595292253522 for SPOC 2-min. Variable depth is not explained by aperture differences alone and favors a blended or systematic false alarm over a stable planet transit.

The star shows a significant out-of-transit swing at this 11.4 d period whose amplitude is ~18% of the dip depth, inconsistent with a flat planetary transit and more consistent with stellar variability or a close binary contamination competing with the transit signal.

Transit fit density does not match the M-dwarf stellar density; high penalty despite a flat-bottom shape (v_sigma -2.852) indicates the duration/radius combination is not self-consistent for a planet on this target.
reasons.value: 55.87 with fit_log_density_ratio -0.6214 vs central duration ratio 1.499

reasons.why: Independent classifier ranks it well below the median planet (0.5) and similar signals have been splits of planets and blends/false alarms, supporting the planet as not the best explanation when combined with the variable depth and phase curve.
